content.text: AAA: Screening: men aged 65 to 75 years who have ever smoked
The USPSTF recommends 1-time screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) w ultrasonography in men aged 65 to 75 years who have ever smoked.
Anxiety Disorders in Adults: Screening: adults 64 years or younger, incl preg and postpartum persons
The USPSTF recommends screening for anxiety disorders in adults, incl preg and postpartum persons.
Anxiety in Children and Adolescents: Screening: children and adolescents aged 8 to 18 years
The USPSTF recommends screening for anxiety in children and adolescents aged 8 to 18 years.
ASA Use to Prevent Preeclampsia and Related Morbidity and Mortality: Preventive med: preg persons @ ↑risk for preeclampsia

The USPSTF recommends the use of low-dose ASA (81 mg/day) as preventive med after 12 wks of gestation in persons who are @ ↑risk for preeclampsia. See the Practice Considerations section for info on ↑risk and ASA dose.
ASx Bacteriuria in Adults: Screening: preg persons
The USPSTF recommends screening for aSx bacteriuria using urine cx in preg persons.
BRCA-Related CA: Risk Assessment, Genetic Counseling, and Genetic Testing: women w a personal or FHx of breast, ovarian, tubal, or peritoneal CA or an ancestry assoc w brca1/2 gene mut

The USPSTF recommends that primary care clinicians assess women w a personal or FHx of breast, ovarian, tubal, or peritoneal CA or who have an ancestry assoc w breast CA suscep 1 and 2 (BRCA1/2) gene mutations w an appropriate brief familial risk assessment tool. Women w a (+) result on the risk assessment tool should receive genetic counseling and, if indicated after counseling, genetic testing.
Breast CA: med Use to Reduce Risk: women @ ↑risk for breast CA aged 35 years or older

The USPSTF recommends that clinicians offer to prescribe risk-reducing meds, such as tamoxifen, raloxifene, or aromatase inhibitors, to women who are @ ↑risk for breast CA and @ ↓risk for adverse med effects.
Breast Cancer: Screening: women aged 40 to 74 years
The USPSTF recommends biennial screening mammography for women aged 40 to 74 years. †
Breastfeed: Primary Care Behavioral Counseling Interventions: preg and postpartum women
The USPSTF recommends providing interventions or referrals, during preg and after birth, to support breastfeed.
Cervical CA: Screening: women aged 21 to 65 years

The USPSTF recommends screening for cervical CA Q3yr w cervical cytology alone in women aged 21 to 29 years. For women aged 30 to 65 years, the USPSTF recommends screening Q3yr w cervical cytology alone, Q5yr w high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) testing alone, or Q5yr w hrHPV testing in combo w cytology (cotesting). See the clin Considerations section for the relative benefits and harms of alt screening strategies for women 21 years or older.
Chlamydia and Gonorrhea: Screening: sexually active women, incl preg persons
The USPSTF recommends screening for gonorrhea in all sexually active women 24 years or younger and in women 25 years or older who are @ ↑risk for infect.
Chlamydia and Gonorrhea: Screening: sexually active women, incl preg persons
The USPSTF recommends screening for chlamydia in all sexually active women 24 years or younger and in women 25 years or older who are @ ↑risk for infect.
CRC: Screening: adults aged 45 to 49 years
The USPSTF recommends screening for CRC in adults aged 45 to 49 years. See the "Practice Considerations" section and Table 1 for details about screening strategies.
CRC: Screening: adults aged 50 to 75 years
The USPSTF recommends screening for CRC in all adults aged 50 to 75 years. See the "Practice Considerations" section and Table 1 for details about screening strategies.
Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening: adults, incl preg and postpartum persons, and older adults (65 years or older)
The USPSTF recommends screening for depression in the adult pop, incl preg and postpartum persons, as well as older adults.
Depression and Suicide Risk in Children and Adolescents: Screening: adolescents aged 12 to 18 years
The USPSTF recommends screening for major depressive disorder (MDD) in adolescents aged 12 to 18 years.
Falls prev in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Interventions: community-dwelling adults 65 years or older
The USPSTF recommends exercise interventions to prevent falls in community-dwelling adults 65 years or older who are @ ↑risk for falls.
Folic Acid Supplementation to Prevent Neural Tube Defects: Preventive Medication: persons who plan to or could become preg
The USPSTF recommends that all persons planning to or who could become preg take a daily supp containing 0.4 to 0.8 mg (400 to 800 mcg) of folic acid.
GDM: Screening: aSx preg persons @ 24 wks of gestation or after
The USPSTF recommends screening for GDM in aSx preg persons @ 24 wks of gestation or after.
Healthy Diet and Physical Activity for CVD prev in Adults w cardiovasc RF: Behavioral Counseling Interventions: adults w CVD RF
The USPSTF recommends offering or referring adults w CVD RF to behavioral counseling interventions to promote a healthy diet and physical activity.
Healthy wt and wt Gain In preg: Behavioral Counseling Interventions: preg persons
The USPSTF recommends that clinicians offer preg persons effective behavioral counseling interventions aimed @ promoting healthy wt gain and preventing excess gestational wt gain in preg.
HBV infect in Adolescents and Adults: Screening: adolescents and adults @ ↑risk for infect

The USPSTF recommends screening for hepatitis B virus (HBV) infect in adolescents and adults @ ↑risk for infect. See the Practice Considerations section for a description of adolescents and adults @ ↑risk for infect.
HBV infect in preg Women: Screening: preg women
The USPSTF recommends screening for hepatitis B virus (HBV) infect in preg women @ their first prenatal visit
HCV infect in Adolescents and Adults: Screening: adults aged 18 to 79 years
The USPSTF recommends screening for hepatitis C virus (HCV) infect in adults aged 18 to 79 years.
High Body Mass Index in Children and Adolescents: Interventions: children and adolescents 6 years or older

The USPSTF recommends that clinicians provide or refer children and adolescents 6 years or older w a ↑body mass index (BMI) (≥95th percentile for age and sex) to comprehensive, intensive behavioral interventions. See the Practice Considerations section for more info about behavioral interventions.
Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infect: Screening: adolescents and adults aged 15 to 65 years

The USPSTF recommends that clinicians screen for HIV infect in adolescents and adults aged 15 to 65 years. Younger adolescents and older adults who are @ ↑risk of infect should also be screened. See the clin Considerations section for more info about assessment of risk, screening intervals, and rescreening in preg.
Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infect: Screening: preg persons
The USPSTF recommends that clinicians screen for HIV infect in all preg persons, incl those who present in labor or @ delivery whose HIV status = unknown.
HTN in Adults: Screening: adults 18 years or older w.o known HTN

The USPSTF recommends screening for HTN in adults 18 years or older w office blood pressure measurement (OBPM). The USPSTF recommends obtaining BP measurements outside of the clin setting for diagnostic confirmation b4 starting tx.
Hypertensive Disorders of preg: Screening: aSx preg persons
The USPSTF recommends screening for hypertensive disorders in preg persons w BP measurements throughout preg.
Intimate Partner Violence and Caregiver Abuse of Older or Vulnerable Adults: Screening: women of reprod age, incl preg and postpartum women

The USPSTF recommends that clinicians screen for intimate partner violence (IPV) in women of reprod age, incl those who are preg and postpartum. See the "Practice Considerations" section for info on evidence-based multicomponent interventions and for info on IPV in men.
Latent TB infect in Adults: Screening: aSx adults @ ↑risk of latent TB infect (ltbi)
The USPSTF recommends screening for LTBI in populations @ ↑risk. See the "Assessment of Risk" section for additional info on adults @ ↑risk.
Lung CA: Screening: adults aged 50 to 80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoke Hx and currently smoke or have quit w.in the past 15 years

The USPSTF recommends annual screening for lung CA w low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) in adults aged 50 to 80 years who have a 20 pack-year smoke Hx and currently smoke or have quit w.in the past 15 years. Screening should be discontinued once a person has ⍉smoked for 15 years or develops a health problem that substantially limits life expectancy or the ability or willingness to have curative lung surg.
Ocular Prophylaxis for Gonococcal Ophthalmia Neonatorum: Preventive med: newborns
The USPSTF recommends prophylactic ocular topical med for all newborns to prevent gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum.
Osteoporosis to Prevent Fractures: Screening: postmenopausal women younger than 65 years w 1 or more RF for osteoporosis

The USPSTF recommends screening for osteoporosis to prevent osteoporotic fractures in postmenopausal women younger than 65 years who are @ ↑risk for an osteoporotic frx as est by clin risk assessment. See the "Practice Considerations" section for more info on risk assessment and screening tests.
Osteoporosis to Prevent Fractures: Screening: women 65 years or older
The USPSTF recommends screening for osteoporosis to prevent osteoporotic fractures in women 65 years or older. See the "Practice Considerations" section for more info on screening tests.
Perinatal Depression: Preventive Interventions: preg and postpartum persons
The USPSTF recommends that clinicians provide or refer preg and postpartum persons who are @ ↑risk of perinatal depression to counseling interventions.
Prediabetes and T2DM: Screening: aSx adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity

The USPSTF recommends screening for prediabetes and T2DM in adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity. Clinicians should offer or refer pts w prediabetes to effective preventive interventions.
Prev of Acquisition of HIV: Preexposure Prophylaxis: adolescents and adults @ ↑risk of hiv

The USPSTF recommends that clinicians prescribe preexposure prophylaxis using effective antiretroviral therapy to persons who are @ ↑risk of HIV acquisition to decrease the risk of acquiring HIV. See the Practice Considerations section for more info about identification of persons @ ↑risk and about effective antiretroviral therapy.
Prev of Dental Caries in Children Younger Than 5 Years: Screening and Interventions: children younger than 5 years
The USPSTF recommends that primary care clinicians apply fluoride varnish to the primary teeth of all infants and children starting @ the age of primary tooth eruption.
Prev of Dental Caries in Children Younger Than 5 Years: Screening and Interventions: children younger than 5 years
The USPSTF recommends that primary care clinicians prescribe oral fluoride supp starting @ age 6 months for children whose H2O supply = deficient in fluoride.
Rh(D) Incompatibility: Screening: preg women, during the first pregnancy-related care visit
The USPSTF strongly recommends Rh(D) blood typing and Ab testing for all preg women during their first visit for pregnancy-related care.
Rh(D) Incompatibility: Screening: unsensitized rh(d)-negative preg women
The USPSTF recommends repeated Rh(D) Ab testing for all unsensitized Rh(D)-negative women @ 24 to 28 wks' gestation, unless the biological father = known to be Rh(D)-negative.
STIs: Behavioral Counseling: sexually active adolescents and adults @ ↑risk

The USPSTF recommends behavioral counseling for all sexually active adolescents and for adults who are @ ↑risk for sexually transmitted infections (STIs). See the Practice Considerations section for more info on populations @ ↑risk for acquiring STIs.
Skin Cancer Prevention: Behavioral Counseling: young adults, adolescents, children, and parents of young children

The USPSTF recommends counseling young adults, adolescents, children, and parents of young children about minimizing exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation for persons aged 6 months to 24 years w fair skin types to reduce their risk of skin CA.
Statin Use for the Primary prev of CVD in Adults: Preventive med: adults aged 40 to 75 years who have 1 or more cardiovasc RF and an est 10-year cardiovascular disease (cvd) risk of 10% or greater

The USPSTF recommends that clinicians prescribe a statin for the primary prev of CVD for adults aged 40 to 75 years who have 1 or more CVD RF (ie dyslipidemia, diabetes, HTN, or smoke) and an est 10-year risk of a cardiovasc event of 10% or greater.
Syphilis infect During preg: Screening: aSx preg women
The USPSTF recommends early, universal screening for syphilis infect during preg; if an individual = ⍉screened early in preg, the USPSTF recommends screening @ the first available opportunity.
Syphilis infect in Nonpregnant Adolescents and Adults: Screening: aSx, nonpregnant adolescents and adults who are @ ↑risk for syphilis infect
The USPSTF recommends screening for syphilis infect in persons who are @ ↑risk for infect.
Tobacco smoke Cessation in Adults, incl preg Persons: Interventions: nonpregnant adults

The USPSTF recommends that clinicians ask all adults about tobacco use, advise them to stop using tobacco, and provide behavioral interventions and US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)--approved pharmacotherapy for cessation to nonpregnant adults who use tobacco.
Tobacco smoke Cessation in Adults, incl preg Persons: Interventions: preg persons
The USPSTF recommends that clinicians ask all preg persons about tobacco use, advise them to stop using tobacco, and provide behavioral interventions for cessation to preg persons who use tobacco.
Tobacco Use in Children and Adolescents: Primary Care Interventions: school-aged children and adolescents who have ⍉started to use tobacco
The USPSTF recommends that primary care clinicians provide interventions, incl education or brief counseling, to prevent initiation of tobacco use among school-aged children and adolescents.
Unhealthy EToH Use in Adolescents and Adults: Screening and Behavioral Counseling Interventions: adults 18 years or older, incl preg women

The USPSTF recommends screening for unhealthy EToH use in primary care settings in adults 18 years or older, incl preg women, and providing persons engaged in risky or hazardous drinking w brief behavioral counseling interventions to reduce unhealthy EToH use.
Unhealthy Drug Use: Screening: adults age 18 years or older

The USPSTF recommends screening by asking questions about unhealthy drug use in adults age 18 years or older. Screening should be implemented when services for accurate dx, effective tx, and appropriate care can be offered or referred. (Screening refers to asking questions about unhealthy drug use, ⍉testing biological specimens.)
Vision in Children Ages 6 Months to 5 Years: Screening: children aged 3 to 5 years
The USPSTF recommends vision screening ± once in all children aged 3 to 5 years to detect amblyopia or its RF.
Wt Loss to Prevent Obesity-Related Morbidity and Mortality in Adults: Behavioral Interventions: adults

The USPSTF recommends that clinicians offer or refer adults w a body mass index (BMI) of 30 or higher (calculated as wt in kilograms ÷ height in meters squared) to intensive, multicomponent behavioral interventions.
